lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Look & write

details: Look and write serves as a comprehensive review of the unit's language. Students must identify health problems and then write the corresponding logical advice, consolidating vocabulary and grammar.
Look for the correct identification and spelling of the illnesses, and the correct and logical advice written for each child.
“Today, we’re not in class. We’re in the hospital clinic! And I’m the doctor. We have three new patients today. Can you help me? I need to know what’s the matter, and then we can choose what to do!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Listen and number.

details: Listen and number assesses students’ listening comprehension of the unit's language in short dialogues. Students must listen to the conversations and number the pictures in the correct sequence.
Look for focused listening and the correct numbers (1-4) written in the boxes corresponding to the sequence of the audio clips.
“I've received some messages from other patients, but they are all mixed up! I really need some help to understand them all.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.87 - A Trace and write.

details: Trace and write consolidates the link between health problems and their corresponding advice. Students trace lines to match the pairs correctly, then write complete sentences to practise the full structure.
Look for correctly traced lines connecting the right problem to the right remedy, and accurately written sentences for both the illness and the advice.
“OK team! There are more sick children. Let’s help them get better as fast as we can! Can you help me write the reports? I need to know what they should do, and what’s wrong!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.87 - B Read and circle.

details: Read and circle is an assessment of the unit's grammar. Students must choose the correct words in each dialogue, demonstrating their understanding of question forms, verb structures, and modals.
Look for accurate circling of the correct grammatical forms and vocabulary in all four dialogues, showing a solid understanding of the unit's key language.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Speaking Doctor and Patient Game

details: The Doctor and Patient Game is a culminating speaking task that synthesizes the unit's language in a communicative role-play. Students interact freely to match problems with advice, encouraging fluent language use.
Look for active participation, confident use of the full dialogue, and students correctly following the game's rules of matching and switching cards when they find the right 'doctor'.

“Our classroom is now a big hospital! Half of you are doctors and half are patients. Patients, you must find a doctor who can help you. Doctors, you must give the right advice. The first person to switch all their cards is the winner!”
